classification.difficultyReason: Combine an absolute-value graph with a reflected exponential graph, preserving the small curved section between two corners.

answer.short:
$$y=\begin{cases}-x+2-2^x,&x<0,\\x+2-2^x,&0\le x\le1,\\x+2^x-2,&x>1.\end{cases}$$

Corners at $(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$, with a small upward bump between them. Add the ordinates of $y=|x|$ and $y=|2^x-2|$.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x|$. Sketch $y=2^x-2$, then reflect its portion below the $x$-axis upwards to obtain $y=|2^x-2|$. Add the ordinates at each $x$.

$$y=\begin{cases}-x+2-2^x,&x<0,\\x+2-2^x,&0\le x\le1,\\x+2^x-2,&x>1.\end{cases}$$

The graph passes through $(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$. At $x=\tfrac12$, $y=\tfrac52-\sqrt2>1$, giving a small bump between these points. The left branch decreases towards $(0,1)$; the branch after $(1,1)$ increases.
